decisions.reason: Its consumer superfood format is far from the firm's core industrial waste-to-nutrient and energy options and likely carries higher marketing and distribution costs, so with many other ventures to fund the option is not worth keeping.
As a modular extension of the core waste-to-energy offer, it shares existing engineering and customer resources, keeping the option cheap while uncertainty about decentralized energy demand remains.
Its dedicated website page signals ongoing commitment and the waste-oil-to-energy option remains strategically valuable amid unresolved regulatory and energy-price uncertainty.

Although plastic-to-fuel faces technical and economic uncertainty, it is close to the firm's established waste conversion capabilities and the sustainability option is worth retaining at low marginal cost.
